Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.sqlite

Class SQLiteQueryGrammar

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.query.QueryGrammar
org.aristonis.diwan.database.sqlite.SQLiteQueryGrammar
public class SQLiteQueryGrammar extends QueryGrammar
Compiles queries into SQLite SQL, a hand port of Laravel's Illuminate\Database\Query\Grammars\SQLiteGrammar.

Differences from the base grammar: SQLite's extra operators, case-sensitive like through glob, is as the null-safe comparison, date wheres through strftime, an update or delete with joins or a limit through a rowid subselect, each union part wrapped as select * from (...), insert or ignore from a subquery, truncate as two deletes, and every Instant binding written as the whole microseconds an instant column stores.

Two limits come from SQLite itself and are not checked here. A right join needs SQLite 3.39 or newer; older SQLite, such as the one in Android 9, refuses it with its own syntax error, which reaches the caller as a QueryException. An update or delete with joins selects the table's rowid, so on a WITHOUT ROWID table it fails the same way, with SQLite's "no such column" error; telling such a table apart would need a schema read on every call.

Laravel's compileLock returns an empty string for SQLite. This grammar does the same for every lock strength with LockWait.WAIT: SQLite has no row locks, so a locked select takes no lock early. A wait that changes behaviour is refused with UnsupportedOperationException.

Instances are immutable and safe to share between threads.

    • whereLike

      protected String whereLike(Builder query, Where.Like where)
      Compiles a like condition; a case-sensitive one becomes glob, since SQLite's like ignores ASCII case.

      The pattern keeps like's wildcards: % and _ are translated to * and ? in SQL, and a * or ? in the pattern matches itself. A [ matches itself too; Laravel leaves it opening a glob character class, so a value such as [a] there matches the text a.

      Parameters:
      query - the query, never null
      where - the condition, never null
      Returns:
      the SQL, never null

    • compileLock

      protected String compileLock(Builder query, RowLock lock)
      Compiles a row lock as nothing. SQLite has no row locks: the select takes no lock early, and the transaction takes the database's write lock only at its first write. On the JDBC driver a transaction starts deferred, so two transactions that read and then update the same row do not queue as they would on PostgreSQL; the second writer fails with a busy error. A wait that changes which rows are read, LockWait.NOWAIT or LockWait.SKIP_LOCKED, is refused, since a caller who asked for it would get a result it did not expect.
      Parameters:
      query - the query, never null
      lock - the lock, never null
      Returns:
      the empty string, never null
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the query has unions
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the wait is not LockWait.WAIT

      public Map<String,List<Object>> compileTruncate(Builder query)
      Compiles the two statements that empty a table: reset its autoincrement counter in sqlite_sequence, then delete every row.

      The counter statement needs sqlite_sequence to exist, which SQLite creates with the first autoincrement table of the database; Diwan's id() column is one.

      Overrides:
      compileTruncate in class QueryGrammar

    • compileTruncateMany

      public Map<String,List<Object>> compileTruncateMany(List<String> tables, boolean cascade)
      Compiles the statements that empty several tables: defer foreign-key checks to the commit, delete every row of each table, then reset their autoincrement counters in sqlite_sequence, one statement for each schema.

      Deferred checks make the order of the tables irrelevant; a table outside the list that still refers to an emptied one makes the commit fail, as PostgreSQL refuses without cascade. The connection-aware overload used by the query factory orders the deletes instead. As with compileTruncate(org.aristonis.diwan.database.query.Builder), the counter statements need sqlite_sequence to exist.

      Overrides:
      compileTruncateMany in class QueryGrammar
      Parameters:
      tables - the table names, never null, optionally schema.table
      cascade - ignored here, as this overload has no connection to find the referring tables; the connection-aware overload used by the query factory empties them too
      Returns:
      the pragma, the deletes, then the counter resets bound to the prefixed table names, in run order, unmodifiable, never null

    • compileTruncateMany

      protected Map<String,List<Object>> compileTruncateMany(List<String> tables, boolean cascade, Connection connection)
      Compiles the statements that empty several tables, leaving out the counter reset of a schema that has no sqlite_sequence yet.

      The deletes are ordered so that a listed table is emptied before any listed table it refers to, read from pragma_foreign_key_list; references to tables outside the list and self-references are ignored. No deferred check is used then, so a table outside the list that still refers to an emptied one fails at its own delete statement, inside the transaction, where the rollback works on every driver.

      When the listed tables refer to each other in a cycle no order exists, and the statements fall back to deferred foreign-key checks. A violation from a table outside the list then shows at commit; on Android a failed commit cannot be rolled back, so list every referring table in that case.

      Parameters:
      tables - the table names, never null, optionally schema.table
      cascade - emulated: when true, every table that refers to a listed one, directly or through other tables, is emptied too, as PostgreSQL's truncate ... cascade does; only tables that start with the table prefix are found. When false, only the listed tables
      connection - the connection the statements will run on, never null
      Returns:
      the statements that apply to this database, in run order, unmodifiable, never null

    • runTruncate

      protected void runTruncate(Connection connection, List<String> tables, Map<String,List<Object>> statements)
      Runs the statements that empty one or more tables. When there are several, they run in one transaction, unless the connection is already inside one. A grammar whose database needs more around the statements, as SQLite does for keys declared on delete restrict, overrides it.
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection to run on, never null
      tables - the table names as the caller gave them, never null, optionally schema.table or with an alias
      statements - each statement mapped to its bindings, in run order, never null
      Implementation Note:
      Outside a transaction, when a listed table has a key declared on delete restrict to a listed table, the statements run with foreign key enforcement switched off on one held connection: SQLite checks such a key row by row, even when deferred, so it would stop the delete of a table that refers to itself. Other keys keep the usual path, so on delete cascade and set null still act. Before the commit, pragma foreign_key_check must show no new violation, so a table outside the list that still refers to an emptied one fails the truncate and undoes it. Inside a transaction SQLite ignores the switch, and such a key still fails.

      public List<Object> prepareBindings(List<?> bindings)

      prepareBindings in class QueryGrammar

      the converted bindings, unmodifiable, never null
